title: Calibration evidence
purpose: Inspect the recorded instrument model, calculate a temporary linear or quadratic fit, and trace the result revisions that use this evidence.
summary: Inspect a recorded curve, its exact standard points and source, and the result revisions linked to it. Use the read-only worksheet to fit a linear or quadratic model.

tasks.title: Check the curve’s source and points
steps: Compare the model, units and source with the laboratory’s instrument record.

tasks.title: Fit the recorded standards
steps: In [[Calibration fit worksheet]], choose [[Model]] and [[Weighting]], then select [[Calculate fit]].
Read the [[Equation]] and fitted coefficients. For a quadratic fit, check [[Direction over recorded range]].
Compare the predicted and observed responses and residuals in [[Standard points]].

tasks.title: Inspect a result that uses this curve
steps: In [[Result revisions using this calibration]], select a sample ID.
Read that revision’s calibration and verification snapshot beside its result.

tasks.title: Record a correction
steps: Return to the batch and select [[Record calibration]] to create a distinct record.
Enter a new revision of the affected result with the intended evidence and reason.

good_to_know: This record is immutable. Recording another curve does not change any existing result or issued report.
The fit is for inspection. Follow the laboratory’s procedure for method acceptance. Both inverse weightings require positive concentrations at every point.
A curve link is optional and explicitly selected for each result revision; it is never inferred for a batch.
A selected verification correction holds submission, approval and release until a new result revision records current evidence.
The people who recorded a selected curve or verification cannot review or release its result.

sections.title: Access and identity
paragraphs: Active staff with an application role can read this page; clients cannot. The header identifies the analytical batch, frozen analyte, method code/version and matrix. The batch link opens the run. Recorded evidence is a record state, not a scientific acceptance decision.

items.label: Calibration reference
items.description: The immutable instrument/run identifier within its batch.

items.label: Calibration time
items.description: The recorded actual calibration event, displayed in laboratory local time with zone.

items.label: Instrument-reported model
items.description: The supplied equation, fit and weighting description stored as instrument evidence.

items.label: Concentration unit / Response unit
items.description: The frozen units for the standard concentrations and instrument responses; no conversion occurs.

items.label: Source reference
items.description: The instrument output or laboratory source that the recorder supplied. The application does not retain an original instrument file here.

items.label: Equipment at recording
items.description: Equipment identity recorded on the batch when the curve was saved, or Not recorded. Later equipment edits do not rewrite this fact.

items.label: Recorded by / Recorded at
items.description: The staff account and time that created this evidence.

sections.title: Calibration fit worksheet
paragraphs: Staff who can read the calibration can use the worksheet. The calculation fits response as a function of concentration by least squares with an intercept. It uses every recorded point, including repeated concentrations, in the frozen units.

A linear fit requires at least two distinct concentrations. A quadratic fit requires at least three. Both inverse weightings require every concentration to be greater than zero. An explicitly empty or unrecognized model or a missing or unrecognized weighting shows a field error. If the points cannot be fitted, Fit unavailable explains why. The recorded points remain visible in each case.

The worksheet output is temporary and lives on this page. Links from result revisions refer to the frozen instrument evidence. Use the laboratory’s procedure and configured QC checks for method acceptance.

items.label: Model
items.description: Choose Linear for a straight line or Quadratic for a second-degree polynomial. Linear is selected when you first open the worksheet and when you follow a worksheet link that specifies only a weighting.

items.label: Weighting
items.description: Choose a weighting for each calculation. Unweighted (equal weights) gives every row the same weight. 1/x (inverse concentration) weights each row by the reciprocal of its concentration. 1/x² (inverse concentration squared) weights each row by the reciprocal of concentration squared.

items.label: Calculate fit
items.description: Calculate using the selected model and weighting. Choose a weighting to see calculated values alongside the recorded evidence. Change either selection and calculate again to compare fits.

items.label: Equation
items.description: A linear fit shows y = slope × x + intercept. A quadratic fit shows y = a × x² + b × x + intercept. Here x is the recorded concentration and y is the predicted instrument response.

items.label: Slope / Linear coefficient (b)
items.description: The coefficient of concentration, expressed in response units per concentration unit. For a straight line, it gives the change in response per unit of concentration everywhere.

items.label: Quadratic coefficient (a)
items.description: The coefficient of concentration squared, expressed in response units per squared concentration unit. It describes the curvature and appears only for a quadratic fit.

items.label: Intercept
items.description: The fitted response at zero concentration, in response units. Calculated values are displayed with up to 12 significant digits. Predictions and residuals use the unrounded coefficients.

items.label: Direction over recorded range
items.description: For a quadratic fit, the unrounded coefficients determine whether the fitted response increases, decreases, stays constant or turns between the lowest and highest recorded concentrations. A stationary endpoint indicates zero slope at that endpoint.

sections.title: Standard points
paragraphs: The record stores 1 to 50 points. The range is an application limit. A successful worksheet fit adds predicted responses and residuals beside the recorded observations.

items.label: Standard
items.description: The supplied standard/source identifier for each point, in entered order.

items.label: Concentration
items.description: Exact supplied decimal text in the frozen concentration unit, including significant trailing zeros. Concentrations cannot be negative.

items.label: Observed response
items.description: Exact supplied decimal text in the frozen response unit. Signed negative responses are allowed.

items.label: Predicted response
items.description: Response calculated from the chosen fit at the recorded concentration, in the frozen response unit.

items.label: Residual
items.description: Observed response minus predicted response, in the frozen response unit. A positive value means the observation is above the prediction. A negative value means it is below.

items.label: Sample
items.description: Lab ID opens the complete result revision history, including the linked revision.

items.label: Analyte
items.description: Frozen analyte on the result revision.

items.label: Revision / Status
items.description: The exact result revision number and workflow state. Earlier revisions remain listed after corrections.

items.label: Calibration verification
items.description: Frozen selected QC label and observation ID, or Not linked. A link never bypasses configured batch QC gates.

items.label: Rows per page / Page links
items.description: Newest entries first. Choose 25, 50 or 100 rows; First, Previous, Next and Last navigate the complete related history. No linked result revisions means no result has explicitly selected this record.

sections.title: History and corrections
paragraphs: The final history panel identifies who recorded the calibration and when. No edit or delete action is available. To correct the evidence, create another calibration reference and then a new result revision with the intended links and reason. Earlier observations, snapshots and issued PDFs remain unchanged.
